<title>Why fuel prices may go higher still</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762315/original/file-20260925-50-ci5zbw.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=0%2C0%2C5000%2C3333&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">Oil-related prices are high, but poised to go even higher.</span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/illustration/businessman-levitating-on-market-trend-in-royalty-free-illustration/1487540755">Afry Harvy/iStock / Getty Images Plus</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>If you think your energy costs are high now, the situation may be about to get a whole lot worse.</p>

<p>With traffic in the Strait of Hormuz – normally the primary route for oil leaving the Middle East – <a href="https://hormuzstraitmonitor.com/">hovering below 15% of prewar levels</a>, oil prices have <a href="https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/future/cl.1/charts?mod=mw_quote_advanced">increased from US$65 a barrel</a> before the conflict in Iran began in February 2026 to more than $100 a barrel in mid-September.</p>

<p>When the U.S. and Israel first attacked Iran, <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/16/oil-prices-iran-war-200-crude-strait-of-hormuz-supply-shock.html">analysts feared prices would soon reach $150</a> or even $200 a barrel. That hasn’t happened yet. But seven months into the conflict, with no clear end in sight, the global oil market has now largely exhausted the safety measures that exist to keep a lid on petroleum prices.</p>

<p>As researchers who study the relationship between <a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=QnWY1B4AAAAJ&amp;hl=en&amp;oi=ao">energy</a> and <a href="https://gufaculty360.georgetown.edu/s/contact/00336000015cyngAAA/gregory-scott-pollock">national security</a>, we have been following these dynamics throughout the conflict, and the oil market is now <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/11/business/diesel-fuel-prices-oil-iran-war.html">showing signs that significant price hikes</a> – and perhaps even shortages – may be on the way.</p>

<h2>The squeeze tightens</h2>

<p>Some oil has been able to make it out of the Persian Gulf despite the closure of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia increased output via its <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/saudi-arabia-restarts-east-west-oil-pipeline-resume-exports-yanbu-sources-say-2026-09-22/">East-West pipeline</a>, which runs from Abqaiq on the Persian Gulf overland to Yanbu on the coast of the Red Sea. At full capacity, that pipeline can carry as much as <a href="https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/17/from-yanbu-to-sohar-tracking-saudi-arabias-alternative-oil-routes">7 million barrels per day</a>, although only about 4 million to 5 million barrels per day are typically exported.</p>

<p>But attacks on the pipeline in mid-September that Saudi Arabia blames on Iran-backed militias based in Iraq <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/saudi-east-west-pipeline-building-up-volumes-loading-yet-resume-sources-say-2026-09-24/">forced the Saudis to temporarily halt oil shipments</a> through that pipeline. The pipeline has now <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/saudi-arabia-restarts-east-west-oil-pipeline-resume-exports-yanbu-sources-say-2026-09-22/">restarted operations</a> at very low volumes, but it will likely take at least six to eight weeks to regain full capacity. Even this short cessation has tightened already constrained oil markets, and the threat of further <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/25/saudi-arabia-intercepts-houthi-missiles-oil-prices-climbs">Houthi attacks on Red Sea oil exports</a> will only add to inflationary pressures.  </p>



<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A map showing options and quantities for Saudi Arabian oil exports." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762318/original/file-20260925-60-40ibut.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Saudi Arabia has options for oil exports, but interruptions in supply affect global markets.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/an-infographic-titled-saudi-arabias-closure-of-the-east-news-photo/2294763614">Murat Usubali/Anadolu via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Meanwhile, in Russia, <a href="https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9/14/why-is-trump-warning-zelenskyy-not-to-hit-russian-diesel-refineries">Ukrainian drone attacks have damaged refineries</a>, reducing Russian production of diesel fuel and <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/russia-set-extend-diesel-export-ban-until-end-october-vedomosti-reports-2026-09-16/">prompting the country to ban exports of it</a>. That has <a href="https://fortune.com/2026/09/05/overlooked-russia-ukraine-war-outsized-impact-energy-diesel-high/">removed another 3%</a> of the global daily supply of diesel, an <a href="https://theconversation.com/trump-speculates-on-diesel-fuel-export-ban-as-high-prices-ripple-across-us-economy-292323">important fuel for trucking and shipping</a>. When diesel costs go up, the result is <a href="https://theconversation.com/iran-war-pushes-diesel-the-economys-lifeblood-to-record-high-prices-with-no-relief-on-the-horizon-292049">inflation in the cost of goods</a> across the global economy.</p>

<h2>Feeling the pinch</h2>

<p>In the U.S., <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/gasbuddyguy.bsky.social/post/3mw4n335qhs2w">47 states experienced record-high diesel prices</a> on Sept. 22, with the national average <a href="https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/">reaching $6.52</a> per gallon.</p>

<p>The high prices prompted President Donald Trump to <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/23/white-house-ban-diesel-01089294">threaten to ban diesel exports</a>, a move analysts suggest <a href="https://gaspriceguy.substack.com/p/why-a-diesel-export-ban-wont-fix">would make matters worse</a> by accentuating global supply shortages and <a href="https://theconversation.com/trump-speculates-on-diesel-fuel-export-ban-as-high-prices-ripple-across-us-economy-292323">driving world prices upward</a>.</p>

<p>Beyond diesel, <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/64f90ab8-5fb0-4594-a900-d03e5ca051e3?syn-25a6b1a6=1">motor oil prices have quadrupled</a>, and supply shortages are starting to take hold. For instance, Costco has <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/64f90ab8-5fb0-4594-a900-d03e5ca051e3?syn-25a6b1a6=1">almost doubled its prices for motor oil</a> and has limited the amount customers can buy. </p>

<p>The upshot from all this is that Americans are spending a lot more on fuel in 2026 as compared to 2025. Between March 1 and late September, Americans <a href="https://patrickdehaan.com/fuelclock.html">spent an additional $72 billion on gasoline</a>  compared to the same period a year ago, as well as $45 billion more on diesel.  That’s $117 billion in additional fuel costs, above and beyond the costs of the war itself, which the Pentagon <a href="https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/18/politics/us-iran-war-cost">estimated at $45 billion</a> as of early September.</p>

<p>These shocks are even more acute outside the United States, which is the world’s largest energy producer. South and Southeast Asian countries, which were more reliant on imports from the Persian Gulf than the United States, were hit hard soon after the war broke out. Some of them have had to <a href="https://www.cfr.org/articles/the-iran-war-turned-asias-fragile-energy-dependence-into-an-emergency">ration fuel</a>, while others enacted emergency measures like shortening the work or school week to <a href="https://theconversation.com/oil-shortages-escalate-from-wars-in-iran-and-ukraine-with-few-signs-of-relief-288858">reduce fuel use</a>. </p>

<p>These challenges are now hitting Europe hard as well. On Sept. 20, some 15% of French service stations had reportedly <a href="https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/21/fuel-runs-dry-at-15-percent-of-french-stations-as-us-diesel">run out of either diesel or gas</a>.</p>

<h2>Limited tools left</h2>

<p>The international community has already taken most of the measures available to curb oil demand and boost its supply. Those moves have reduced the scale of oil price increases, but they did not prevent them entirely. Now, the toolbox is largely empty, leaving prices on the brink of spiking again.  </p>

<p>In March 2026, a coordinated effort among 32 countries <a href="https://theconversation.com/over-400-million-barrels-will-be-added-to-the-oil-market-soon-what-are-strategic-reserves-and-what-can-they-do-278370">released more than 400 million barrels of oil</a> into the global market from those countries’ strategic reserves. Those stockpiles are now substantially depleted, and it is not clear how much additional oil that countries will be willing or even able to release as the war continues.</p>

<p>Since the war began, the United States alone has <a href="https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&amp;s=WCSSTUS1&amp;f=W">released 130 million barrels</a>, leaving its reserves at a <a href="https://www.npr.org/2026/08/16/nx-s1-5930403/u-s-oil-reserves-hit-the-lowest-level-seen-in-over-40-years">40-year low</a>. The U.S. may not be able to release much more without compromising the <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/15/strategic-petroleum-reserve-spr-oil-iran-war-caverns.html">structural integrity of the salt caverns</a> where the Strategic Petroleum Reserve is stored.</p>

<p><iframe id="Bjevj" class="tc-infographic-datawrapper" src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/Bjevj/1/" height="400px" width="100%" style="border: 0;" scrolling="no" frameborder="0" title="A line chart showing the level of the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve inventory over time."></iframe></p>

<h2>The role of China</h2>

<p><a href="https://www.theatlantic.com/economy/2026/07/china-iran-usa-oil-prices/688086/">China</a> has played the largest role in containing global oil prices to date by releasing official reserves as well as what now seem to be massive <a href="https://www.theatlantic.com/economy/2026/07/china-iran-usa-oil-prices/688086/">additional reserves not previously disclosed to the public</a>. The country reduced its <a href="https://www.wsj.com/business/energy-oil/see-how-china-weathered-the-iran-oil-shock-2c367cd8">crude oil imports by nearly 50%</a> between February and June 2026.</p>

<p>The increased electrification of the Chinese economy played a key role in reducing <a href="https://www.energypolicy.columbia.edu/implications-of-the-conflict-in-the-middle-east-for-chinas-energy-security">Chinese demand for oil</a> during this period. <a href="https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-14/china-nevs-top-60-of-new-car-sales-as-exports-offset-domestic-slump-102473923.html">More than 60% of new passenger car sales</a> in China are electric vehicles or plug-in hybrids, and <a href="https://www.scmp.com/economy/china-economy/article/3361383/how-china-rolling-out-electric-trucks-vast-scale-boost-net-zero-push">30% of its heavy truck sales</a> are now electric.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A person plugs a car into a charging station." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=360&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=360&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=360&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=452&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=452&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762320/original/file-20260925-60-dig096.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=452&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">China has worked very hard over many years to boost the number of electric cars on the country’s roads.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/the-car-owner-is-charging-the-electric-vehicle-at-the-state-news-photo/2295618706">CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Overall, China’s electrification of its transport sector allowed it to <a href="https://oilprice.com/Energy/Energy-General/Chinas-EV-Boom-Is-Quietly-Undermining-Oils-Biggest-Chokepoint.html">reduce oil consumption by 1.35 million barrels per day</a> in the first half of 2026.</p>

<p>Other countries are <a href="https://foreignpolicy.com/2026/03/06/iran-china-green-energy-oil-gas-hormuz-solar-electricity/">looking to China</a> for help as well. The country’s international <a href="https://edition.cnn.com/2026/04/26/energy/china-clean-energy-exports-intl-hnk">sales of electric vehicles, batteries and solar panels have skyrocketed</a>, as other countries seek to insulate themselves from oil market shocks. </p>

<p>Less encouragingly when it comes to greenhouse gas emissions, China has <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/chinas-coal-power-rise-again-2026-reversing-first-in-a-decade-decline-2026-06-24/">used more coal</a> to offset oil demand and as an alternative means of petrochemical production as well.  </p>

<p>Of perhaps more immediate concern, China’s oil demand is now starting to creep up again, <a href="https://www.scmp.com/economy/china-economy/article/3368047/chinas-crude-imports-are-rising-again-what-will-mean-oil-prices">with crude imports rising 6.2% in August 2026</a> as compared with the previous month. Even if its imports don’t reach prewar levels any time soon, increased Chinese demand, coupled with a tighter oil market, may result in additional price hikes over the next few weeks.</p>

<p>China still has about four to six months of stockpiles, including commercial and strategic reserves, but Beijing may soon seek to gradually <a href="https://www.kpler.com/blog/why-the-real-oil-shock-may-only-begin-when-china-returns">restock its inventories</a>, although the Chinese may postpone these purchases if prices continue to soar.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="Cars line up at a gas station." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=399&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=399&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=399&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=501&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=501&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762319/original/file-20260925-50-g135i7.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=501&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">In France, lines at gas stations in 2026 are similar to 1970s lines in the U.S., with customers lining up in hope of getting fuel before it runs out.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/cars-queue-at-a-totalenergies-service-station-in-fleury-les-news-photo/2296009549">Romain Gautier/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<h2>A look ahead</h2>

<p>Sustained conflict in Iran – <a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/an-overview-irans-energy-industry-infrastructure-2026-02-28/">itself a major oil producer</a> – continued disruptions of oil shipments in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran-linked militias’ <a href="https://africacenter.org/spotlight/2026-houthi-red-sea-threats/">disruptions to shipping in the Red Sea</a> could mean the reemergence of the <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/16/oil-prices-iran-war-200-crude-strait-of-hormuz-supply-shock.html">nightmare scenarios analysts envisioned</a> when the fighting began. </p>

<p>It’s not clear if that would translate into simply much higher prices at the pump or turn into <a href="https://www.ineteconomics.org/perspectives/blog/oil-and-the-energy-crisis-of-the-1970s-a-reanalysis">1970s-style shortages</a>, where there’s not enough fuel available at any price and lines stretch around the block at gas stations.</p>

<p>With the 2026 midterm elections looming, the White House will want to avoid that scenario at all costs. But the Trump administration has already <a href="https://www.npr.org/2026/09/25/nx-s1-5965797/strategic-petroleum-reserve-low-level-venezuela">released large amounts from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve</a> and has rejected policies that would have reduced oil demand, such as stricter <a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/us-announce-sharply-lower-vehicle-fuel-economy-requirements-2026-08-31/">fuel economy standards</a> or incentives for <a href="https://www.usatoday.com/story/cars/shopping/evs/2026/09/22/ev-sales-year-after-trump-ended-tax-credits/91887066007/">electric vehicle</a> adoption.   </p>

<p>At this point, Trump has relatively few options available to blunt new price shocks, the effects of which may be visible not just at the pump but also at the ballot box.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/292853/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

body: Oil-related prices are high, but poised to go even higher
Afry Harvy/iStock / Getty Images Plus If you think your energy costs are high now, the situation may be about to get a whole lot worse

With traffic in the Strait of Hormuz – normally the primary route for oil leaving the Middle East – hovering below 15% of prewar levels , oil prices have increased from US$65 a barrel before the conflict in Iran began in February 2026 to more than $100 a barrel in mid-September
When the U.S. and Israel first attacked Iran, analysts feared prices would soon reach $150 or even $200 a barrel
But seven months into the conflict, with no clear end in sight, the global oil market has now largely exhausted the safety measures that exist to keep a lid on petroleum prices

As researchers who study the relationship between energy and national security , we have been following these dynamics throughout the conflict, and the oil market is now showing signs that significant price hikes – and perhaps even shortages – may be on the way
The squeeze tightens Some oil has been able to make it out of the Persian Gulf despite the closure of Hormuz
Saudi Arabia increased output via its East-West pipeline , which runs from Abqaiq on the Persian Gulf overland to Yanbu on the coast of the Red Sea
At full capacity, that pipeline can carry as much as 7 million barrels per day , although only about 4 million to 5 million barrels per day are typically exported
But attacks on the pipeline in mid-September that Saudi Arabia blames on Iran-backed militias based in Iraq forced the Saudis to temporarily halt oil shipments through that pipeline
The pipeline has now restarted operations at very low volumes, but it will likely take at least six to eight weeks to regain full capacity
Even this short cessation has tightened already constrained oil markets, and the threat of further Houthi attacks on Red Sea oil exports will only add to inflationary pressures
Saudi Arabia has options for oil exports, but interruptions in supply affect global markets

Murat Usubali/Anadolu via Getty Images Meanwhile, in Russia, Ukrainian drone attacks have damaged refineries , reducing Russian production of diesel fuel and prompting the country to ban exports of it
That has removed another 3% of the global daily supply of diesel, an important fuel for trucking and shipping
When diesel costs go up, the result is inflation in the cost of goods across the global economy
Feeling the pinch In the U.S., 47 states experienced record-high diesel prices on Sept. 22, with the national average reaching $6.52 per gallon

The high prices prompted President Donald Trump to threaten to ban diesel exports , a move analysts suggest would make matters worse by accentuating global supply shortages and driving world prices upward
Beyond diesel, motor oil prices have quadrupled , and supply shortages are starting to take hold
For instance, Costco has almost doubled its prices for motor oil and has limited the amount customers can buy
The upshot from all this is that Americans are spending a lot more on fuel in 2026 as compared to 2025
Between March 1 and late September, Americans spent an additional $72 billion on gasoline compared to the same period a year ago, as well as $45 billion more on diesel
That’s $117 billion in additional fuel costs, above and beyond the costs of the war itself, which the Pentagon estimated at $45 billion as of early September
These shocks are even more acute outside the United States, which is the world’s largest energy producer
South and Southeast Asian countries, which were more reliant on imports from the Persian Gulf than the United States, were hit hard soon after the war broke out
Some of them have had to ration fuel , while others enacted emergency measures like shortening the work or school week to reduce fuel use
These challenges are now hitting Europe hard as well
On Sept. 20, some 15% of French service stations had reportedly run out of either diesel or gas
Limited tools left The international community has already taken most of the measures available to curb oil demand and boost its supply
Those moves have reduced the scale of oil price increases, but they did not prevent them entirely
Now, the toolbox is largely empty, leaving prices on the brink of spiking again
In March 2026, a coordinated effort among 32 countries released more than 400 million barrels of oil into the global market from those countries’ strategic reserves
Those stockpiles are now substantially depleted, and it is not clear how much additional oil that countries will be willing or even able to release as the war continues
Since the war began, the United States alone has released 130 million barrels , leaving its reserves at a 40-year low
The U.S. may not be able to release much more without compromising the structural integrity of the salt caverns where the Strategic Petroleum Reserve is stored

The role of China China has played the largest role in containing global oil prices to date by releasing official reserves as well as what now seem to be massive additional reserves not previously disclosed to the public
The country reduced its crude oil imports by nearly 50% between February and June 2026
The increased electrification of the Chinese economy played a key role in reducing Chinese demand for oil during this period
More than 60% of new passenger car sales in China are electric vehicles or plug-in hybrids, and 30% of its heavy truck sales are now electric
China has worked very hard over many years to boost the number of electric cars on the country’s roads

title: Are there toxic chemicals in your grocery store receipt?
url:
<title>Are there toxic chemicals in your grocery store receipt?</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/761999/original/file-20260924-50-1mryfp.jpeg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=0%2C1%2C7952%2C5301&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">Receipts are printed on thermal paper, which often contains bisphenols.</span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/photo/hands-exchanging-receipt-at-supermarket-checkout-royalty-free-image/2215927944">alvarez/E+ via Getty Images</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>“Would you like your receipt?” </p>

<p>It’s a question you’re likely to hear every time you pop into the grocery store or stop for a latte on the way to work. Some people may also have heard warnings that have circulated for more than 15 years that if you say yes, toxic chemicals might rub off on your fingertips. </p>

<p>As a recent example, a 2025 study from the Center for Environmental Health, a nonprofit advocacy organization focused on toxic chemicals in consumer products, claimed that <a href="https://ceh.org/latest/press-releases/touching-1-receipt-for-10-seconds-results-in-exposure-to-the-chemical-bps-above-the-safe-limit/">holding a paper receipt for only 10 seconds</a> could result in exposure to unsafe levels of toxic chemicals. </p>

<p>Could something so commonplace really be slowly poisoning people? </p>

<p>I am a <a href="https://chicago.medicine.uic.edu/emergency-medicine/profiles/mccann-sean/">medical toxicologist</a> – a physician who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of poisoning. I see patients in my clinic for everything from severe lead poisoning to questions about exposure to chemicals that are mostly harmless. </p>

<p>Receipts are printed on a special type of paper – thermal paper – which often contains chemicals called bisphenols. These chemicals are potentially – but not necessarily – toxic. So, like many questions in toxicology, the answer to whether receipts are dangerous to handle is: It depends. </p>

<h2>What are bisphenols and where are they found?</h2>

<p>Bisphenols are <a href="https://www.britannica.com/science/bisphenol-A">human-made chemicals</a> that have been widely used in industrial manufacturing since the 1950s. </p>

<p>Several different types exist, each with a letter standing for the chemical they are made from. The bisphenol produced using a molecule called acetone is called bisphenol A, or BPA. Bisphenol S (BPS) is made using a sulfur atom, and bisphenol F (BPF) is made using formaldehyde. </p>

<p>These chemicals are used to create a type of transparent and shatter-resistant plastic called polycarbonate, found in products including hard plastic water bottles, food storage containers and eyeglass lenses. Bisphenols are also ingredients in epoxy resins, which are used to coat the inside of bottle caps and metal food and drink containers. Some products still use these chemicals, though many manufacturers have phased them out.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="Baby holding a bottle" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/762072/original/file-20260924-50-bmxmai.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Baby bottles no longer contain bisphenol A.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/photo/mother-holding-daughter-drinking-from-bottle-eyes-royalty-free-image/200267737-001">Ryuichi Sato/The Image Bank via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Thermal receipt paper uses bisphenol – usually BPA or BPS – as a developer. The bisphenol is combined with a colorless ink and applied as a microscopic, heat-sensitive film to the paper. Instead of using ink, a receipt printer applies heat to this thermal paper, causing the bisphenol and the dye to react and changing the dye from colorless to black. Fax machines, back in the day, also relied on this technology.</p>

<h2>How do bisphenols affect the human body?</h2>

<p>Toxicologists classify bisphenols as toxins called <a href="https://www.niehs.nih.gov/health/topics/agents/endocrine">endocrine disruptors</a>. This means that they <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envres.2023.116900">interfere with the body’s endocrine system</a>, which controls vital body functions like growth, reproduction and metabolism. </p>

<p>The <a href="https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21201-endocrine-system">endocrine system</a> includes multiple organs, including the thyroid, pancreas and pituitary gland, which is a tiny structure at the base of the brain. These organs send messages throughout the body to control many vital functions, and the molecules that carry that message are called hormones. </p>

<p>Most research on <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.reprotox.2013.08.008">bisphenol toxicity</a> has focused on BPA. Research shows that BPA interrupts the messaging sent through multiple hormones, but <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.yhbeh.2017.11.001">most notably through estrogen</a>. </p>

<p>Many people think of estrogen as the “female” hormone, but all people make estrogen, no matter what sex chromosomes they have. Estrogen helps <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-1031-1_19">control the growth and development of organs</a> as they first form during fetal development, among other important roles in the body.</p>

<p>That’s why exposure to endocrine disruptors is potentially more serious for a developing fetus than it is for adults. BPA exposure has been linked to <a href="https://doi.org/10.1039/d5va00145e">preterm birth and abnormal fetal brain development</a></p>

<p>Exposure to high amounts of BPA could also increase a person’s chances of developing heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envres.2023.116900">and other health problems</a>. Research also shows that BPA can cause oxidative stress – chemical damage to the molecules that make up cells. Exposure to BPA might also cause <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.etap.2024.104467">changes to how genes are turned on or off</a>, and some of these changes can be passed on to future generations. </p>

<p>These findings have led to a <a href="https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/eu-prohibition-use-and-trade-bisphenol-20-january-2025">ban on BPA in Europe</a>. In the United States, its use is <a href="https://abcnews.com/Business/fda-officially-bans-bpa-bisphenol-baby-bottles/story?id=16799087">banned in baby bottles</a>, but no ban exists for most other products. However, many manufacturers have <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sustainable-business/2016/mar/31/bpa-chemical-canned-food-general-mills-campbells-soup-del-monte-fda">voluntarily replaced BPA</a> with alternative chemicals – you have probably seen plastic products advertised as “BPA free.”  </p>

<p>Unfortunately, companies often simply switch out BPA for another bisphenol, such as BPS, and it turns out that BPS shares much of its cousin molecule’s <a href="https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.1408989">toxic traits</a>. Recently, though, concern about all bisphenols has led many companies to move away from them entirely.  </p>

<p>Research has also shown that bisphenols can be absorbed through the skin – for example, when handling a receipt printed on thermal paper. Touching bisphenols with greasy hands, perhaps because you’ve just applied moisturizer or hand sanitizer, can <a href="https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0110509">increase absorption through the skin</a>. </p>

<h2>What’s the dose?</h2>

<p>You have probably heard the old saying “the dose makes the poison.” This is a foundational principle of toxicology originally written by the Swiss physician and chemist <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/bcpt.12622">Paracelsus in 1538</a>.</p>

<p>Consider <a href="https://wwwn.cdc.gov/tsp/ToxFAQs/ToxFAQsDetails.aspx?faqid=71&amp;toxid=19">the classic poison cyanide</a>. A dose capable of killing an average person weighs less than 10 grains of rice. However, the human body actually makes tiny amounts of cyanide every day. A natural detoxification system clears it out of the body so it causes no harm. </p>

<p>Similarly, though we all require a fair amount of water every day to survive, there is such a thing as <a href="https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/water-intoxication">water toxicity</a>. Too much water can cause your brain to swell and can be fatal, as <a href="https://archive.nytimes.com/thelede.blogs.nytimes.com/2007/01/15/too-high-a-price-for-a-wii">several tragic cases</a> over the years have shown. </p>

<figure>
            <iframe width="440" height="260" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/NacigUzvAo4?wmode=transparent&amp;start=0" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>
            <figcaption><span class="caption">Reducing exposure is more important than avoiding any one thing.</span></figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>In 2023, researchers estimated the daily “dose” of exposure to BPA from thermal paper receipts and found levels somewhere between about <a href="https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0283675">5,000 to 50 million times lower</a> than European Food Safety Authority standards. That’s less than one drop in an 8-ounce glass of water. </p>

<p>That said, this estimate is for the average person. Retail, food service and other workers who handle many receipts every day would be exposed to doses about 100 times higher than that, the researchers estimated. This is potentially more concerning, but still probably well below safety standard levels. </p>

<p>Bisphenols are found in many products and do have potential to harm our health, but most human exposure to these chemicals <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2015.01.008">comes from food or beverages</a> packaged in containers made with bisphenols. Exposure from handling receipts is a small piece of the pie. </p>

<h2>Taking reasonable precautions</h2>

<p>The upshot is that for most people, handling receipts is a pretty low-risk activity. But if you’re concerned, you can take a few straightforward precautions.</p>

<p>People who handle receipts at work could protect themselves by avoiding the use of sanitizer and other skin care products on their hands before work, wearing gloves or encouraging their employer to use bisphenol-free thermal paper. </p>

<p>People who might be sensitive to endocrine effects of bisphenols – pregnant people, infants, children and those with certain endocrine diseases – might want to avoid contact with thermal paper receipts.</p>

<p>For people outside of these sensitive groups, handling a receipt is probably a very low-risk activity. But if you are concerned, some commonsense strategies that could minimize your exposure include opting for emailed receipts when available, or tucking a printed receipt into a bag or pocket rather than holding on to it for a prolonged period of time. </p>

<p>Personally, I avoid paper receipts for the most part – I don’t like making extra trash.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/291246/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

body: Receipts are printed on thermal paper, which often contains bisphenols. alvarez/E+ via Getty Images “Would you like your receipt?” It’s a question you’re likely to hear every time you pop into the grocery store or stop for a latte on the way to work
Some people may also have heard warnings that have circulated for more than 15 years that if you say yes, toxic chemicals might rub off on your fingertips

As a recent example, a 2025 study from the Center for Environmental Health, a nonprofit advocacy organization focused on toxic chemicals in consumer products, claimed that holding a paper receipt for only 10 seconds could result in exposure to unsafe levels of toxic chemicals
Could something so commonplace really be slowly poisoning people? I am a medical toxicologist – a physician who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of poisoning
I see patients in my clinic for everything from severe lead poisoning to questions about exposure to chemicals that are mostly harmless
Receipts are printed on a special type of paper – thermal paper – which often contains chemicals called bisphenols
These chemicals are potentially – but not necessarily – toxic
So, like many questions in toxicology, the answer to whether receipts are dangerous to handle is: It depends
What are bisphenols and where are they found? Bisphenols are human-made chemicals that have been widely used in industrial manufacturing since the 1950s
Several different types exist, each with a letter standing for the chemical they are made from
The bisphenol produced using a molecule called acetone is called bisphenol A, or BPA
Bisphenol S (BPS) is made using a sulfur atom, and bisphenol F (BPF) is made using formaldehyde

These chemicals are used to create a type of transparent and shatter-resistant plastic called polycarbonate, found in products including hard plastic water bottles, food storage containers and eyeglass lenses
Bisphenols are also ingredients in epoxy resins, which are used to coat the inside of bottle caps and metal food and drink containers
Some products still use these chemicals, though many manufacturers have phased them out
Baby bottles no longer contain bisphenol A
Ryuichi Sato/The Image Bank via Getty Images Thermal receipt paper uses bisphenol – usually BPA or BPS – as a developer
The bisphenol is combined with a colorless ink and applied as a microscopic, heat-sensitive film to the paper
Instead of using ink, a receipt printer applies heat to this thermal paper, causing the bisphenol and the dye to react and changing the dye from colorless to black
Fax machines, back in the day, also relied on this technology
How do bisphenols affect the human body? Toxicologists classify bisphenols as toxins called endocrine disruptors
This means that they interfere with the body’s endocrine system , which controls vital body functions like growth, reproduction and metabolism
The endocrine system includes multiple organs, including the thyroid, pancreas and pituitary gland, which is a tiny structure at the base of the brain
These organs send messages throughout the body to control many vital functions, and the molecules that carry that message are called hormones
Most research on bisphenol toxicity has focused on BPA
Research shows that BPA interrupts the messaging sent through multiple hormones, but most notably through estrogen
Many people think of estrogen as the “female” hormone, but all people make estrogen, no matter what sex chromosomes they have
Estrogen helps control the growth and development of organs as they first form during fetal development, among other important roles in the body
That’s why exposure to endocrine disruptors is potentially more serious for a developing fetus than it is for adults

BPA exposure has been linked to preterm birth and abnormal fetal brain development Exposure to high amounts of BPA could also increase a person’s chances of developing heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity and other health problems
Research also shows that BPA can cause oxidative stress – chemical damage to the molecules that make up cells
Exposure to BPA might also cause changes to how genes are turned on or off , and some of these changes can be passed on to future generations
These findings have led to a ban on BPA in Europe
In the United States, its use is banned in baby bottles , but no ban exists for most other products

However, many manufacturers have voluntarily replaced BPA with alternative chemicals – you have probably seen plastic products advertised as “BPA free.” Unfortunately, companies often simply switch out BPA for another bisphenol, such as BPS, and it turns out that BPS shares much of its cousin molecule’s toxic traits
Recently, though, concern about all bisphenols has led many companies to move away from them entirely
Research has also shown that bisphenols can be absorbed through the skin – for example, when handling a receipt printed on thermal paper
Touching bisphenols with greasy hands, perhaps because you’ve just applied moisturizer or hand sanitizer, can increase absorption through the skin

What’s the dose? You have probably heard the old saying “the dose makes the poison.” This is a foundational principle of toxicology originally written by the Swiss physician and chemist Paracelsus in 1538
A dose capable of killing an average person weighs less than 10 grains of rice

<title>Generous paternal leave policies improve maternal and newborn health, family finances and workplace equality</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/761311/original/file-20260921-50-skc55i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=0%2C6%2C5506%2C3670&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">Paid leave gives fathers time to bond with their children and improves their mental health.</span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/photo/father-on-paternity-leave-looking-after-his-infant-royalty-free-image/2189580715?phrase=paternity%20leave&amp;adppopup=true">Piksel/iStock via Getty Images Plus</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>When our second child was born, my spouse had several weeks of paternity leave under his parental leave policy at work. </p>

<p>I’m a <a href="https://www.ncfr.org/cfle-certification">certified family life educator</a>, and parental leave comes up regularly in my teaching and community work. So I was aware of <a href="https://getbenepass.com/blog/paternity-leave-benefits">the benefits his leave could have</a> for our family – in theory.</p>

<p>Still, I could not have imagined how significantly his leave would end up affecting our family and our connections with community.</p>

<p>During his leave time, my spouse took our oldest child to playdates and birthday parties. He quickly became connected with our small-town network of families with kids close in age. I witnessed my spouse becoming more comfortable being the “main” parent in public, going to kid-centered community events and connecting with other parents.</p>

<p>Our family is still seeing the benefits of those few weeks 10 years later.</p>

<p>Leave for supporting parents after the birth of a child <a href="https://bipartisanpolicy.org/explainer/state-paid-family-leave-laws-across-the-u-s/">isn’t standardized or required by law</a> in most places in the U.S. Even countries with generous paid time off for the birthing parent <a href="https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/paid-leave-for-fathers_07442bed-en/full-report.html">don’t always offer similarly generous time</a> for the non-birthing parent. </p>

<p>This diversity in leave policies can make it hard to assess the impact of leave for the non-birthing parent. But existing research suggests that extended leave for birthing parents and moderate leave for non-birthing partners <a href="https://policycentermmh.org/the-interconnection-of-paid-family-and-medical-leave-and-maternal-mental-health/#29c3d5a0-dd90-44d9-99e8-bc3b62fe8108-link">positively impact infant well-being</a> and reduce postpartum mental health challenges.</p>

<h2>Maternal and newborn health</h2>

<p>Leave for both parents with the birth of a child can significantly benefit <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amepre.2021.03.018">parental mental health overall</a> and <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(22)00311-5">maternal mental health specifically</a>. Paternity leave <a href="https://blogs.bcm.edu/2026/03/02/the-importance-of-parental-leave/">assists in the mother’s recovery</a> and contributes to <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/s10826-021-02139-3">less of an increase in stress and depression</a> than for mothers whose partners didn’t take leave.</p>

<p>One Swedish study showed that flexibility within paternal leave policies, such as allowing new dads to take intermittent time off after the birth of a child, helped <a href="https://doi.org/10.1257/app.20220400">reduce the incidence of maternal postpartum health complications</a>.</p>

<p>Children also benefit from paternity leave. When a father takes significant leave – meaning at least two weeks – children report <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/s11199-019-01050-y">experiencing more father-child closeness</a> and better communication in the relationship up to nine years later. And <a href="https://doi.org/10.1002%2Fhec.4947">overall child health tends to improve</a> when fathers take paternity leave.</p>

<p>When paid leave policies are <a href="https://doi.org/10.1097/aog.0000000000005502">available for both mothers</a> <a href="https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-025-22013-x">and fathers</a>, breastfeeding is more likely to last longer. Longer breastfeeding is strongly linked to <a href="https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2025-071516">overall infant health</a> and <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amepre.2023.05.015">decreased infant mortality</a>. </p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="two dads walking their babies in strollers" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/761314/original/file-20260921-60-rjslta.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Paternity leave is an opportunity for fathers to become comfortable in their parenting role and connect with other parents.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/photo/male-friends-out-with-their-babies-in-tynemouth-uk-royalty-free-image/1132265388?phrase=paternity%20leave&amp;adppopup=true">SolStock/E+ via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<h2>Family balance</h2>

<p>Allowing both parents to have sufficient time off to bond and adjust to their new roles can also have <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/sjop.70030">longer-term benefits</a> within the family unit and contribute toward more equity in child rearing. Even in 2026, mothers are often considered the “default” parent, with <a href="https://thegepi.org/GEPI-Free-Time-Gender-Gap-Report.pdf">fathers taking a more secondary role</a>.</p>

<p>While <a href="https://www.derekthompson.org/p/why-do-richer-dads-spend-more-time#footnote-1">fathers are more involved</a> now than in previous generations, mothers are <a href="https://theconversation.com/better-call-mom-schools-still-see-mothers-as-the-default-parent-to-contact-288478">still more likely</a> to be the <a href="https://doi-org.proxy.lib.miamioh.edu/10.1093/qje/qjaf027">first call from school</a>. And even with an involved father, mothers continue to carry the invisible <a href="https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/the-compassionate-brain/202412/mental-load-the-invisible-weight-of-parenthood">mental load of the family</a>, an unseen burden of data, obligations and preemptive planning tasks. This overreliance on mothers comes with a price: Mothers report being <a href="https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2023/01/PST_2023.01.24_parenting_REPORT.pdf">more stressed and tired</a> than fathers do.</p>

<p>As I experienced in my own family, when fathers have ample time off, it sets up the dynamic <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-0009.12590">to be more balanced</a> between parents. This helps reduce the strain on recovering mothers and redistributes some of the care work that goes into raising children.</p>

<h2>Home economics</h2>

<p>What’s more, paid leave policies have been shown to help <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-0009.12340">families’ financial health</a>. Pay rates during leave can vary widely depending on your company, organization or country. Without full or close to full pay, many families cannot afford to take leave.</p>

<p>In the U.S., for example, the Family and Medical Leave Act <a href="https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/benefits-leave/fmla">allows time off, but not in all circumstances</a>, nor is that time required to be paid. Many families cannot afford to take the full allowable time off, using up sick or vacation time if available. Many parents in the U.S. end up going back to work <a href="https://nationalpartnership.org/report/paid-leave-is-essential-for/">sooner than seems healthy</a>. </p>

<p>New parents in the U.S. often find themselves in an economic bind – they can’t afford to take leave, nor can they afford to rely on a single income to have a parent stay home. But many also can’t afford the childcare rates for newborns, which tend to be particularly high. National averages for infant care at childcare centers are <a href="https://daycarecalc.com/cost-by-age">nearly US$200 more per month</a> than toddler care. While <a href="https://www.dol.gov/agencies/wb/topics/childcare/price-by-age-care-setting-2022">rates vary significantly</a> depending on where you live and what type of care you choose, <a href="https://finance.yahoo.com/news/much-child-care-costs-every-191603871.html">infant care remains the most expensive</a>.</p>

<p>Despite the lack of a paid U.S. federal leave policy for parents, both domestic and multinational companies have noticed that their workers care about parental leave policies. Some have begun to <a href="https://nationalpartnership.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/new-and-expanded-employer-paid-family-leave-policies.pdf">offer leave for supporting parents</a> in order to <a href="https://doi.org/10.1080/13229400.2025.2536634">recruit and retain workers</a>.</p>

<p><iframe id="F9nD4" class="tc-infographic-datawrapper" src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/F9nD4/2/" height="400px" width="100%" style="border: 0;" scrolling="no" frameborder="0" title="Bar chart showing leave earmarked for mothers, fathers and shareable leave for each of the 38 Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development countries."></iframe></p>

<h2>Outside the US</h2>

<p>U.S. leave policies <a href="https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/5c42d_v1">consistently rank at or near the bottom</a> when compared with other similarly developed countries, like the 38 members of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, or OECD.</p>

<p>Some countries follow a “use-it-or-lose-it” model of parental leave, where fathers in particular are encouraged to take a more substantial role in childcare. Sweden and Norway, for example, earmark <a href="https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/5c42d_v1">90 days of leave</a> for each parent, and it cannot be transferred to or split with the other parent. This encourages both parents to take time off.</p>

<p>There are many options across countries with parental leave policies. <a href="https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/5c42d_v1">Flexibility and defined expectations</a> seem to be key contributors to getting the most out of the parental leave that is offered. </p>

<h2>Cultural adoption</h2>

<p>When non-birthing parents are men, another barrier to taking leave is the perceived social acceptability within their communities. Even when paid paternity leave is available, many men struggle to take it because of how traditional gender roles and expectations of masculinity frame <a href="https://doi.org/10.1037/men0000400">childcare as women’s work</a>. </p>

<p>To offset these kinds of social pressures, countries like <a href="https://www.leavenetwork.org/fileadmin/user_upload/k_leavenetwork/country_notes/2018/FINAL.Japan2018.pdf">Japan</a> and <a href="https://www.oesterreich.gv.at/en/themen/familie_und_partnerschaft/geburt-eines-kindes/1/1/Seite.080522">Austria</a> offer incentives such as bonus leave time for families when fathers actually take their available leave. Germany offers a similar bonus, and it has found <a href="https://doi.org/10.1177/09589287211056187">improved couple relationship satisfaction</a> when fathers take more of their leave time.</p>

<p>Beyond improvements in maternal and infant health, both parents taking leave can <a href="https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/joining-forces-for-gender-equality_67d48024-en/full-report.html">create a more equitable workplace environment</a>. Disparities and discrimination that come when only women take leave after birth can lessen when fathers and other supporting parents also take leave. Childbearing women are then less likely to be penalized, formally or informally, for taking parental leave.</p>

<p>Paid parental leave policies that provide leave for all parents, regardless of gender, also can help <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-0009.12590">reduce structural inequality</a> in the workplace across race and class. In the U.S., <a href="https://www.bls.gov/opub/mlr/2019/article/racial-and-ethnic-disparities-in-access-to-and-use-of-paid-family-and-medical-leave.htm">Hispanic and Black workers often have less access</a> to paid leave policies and may experience increased pressure to return to work earlier than their white counterparts.</p>

<p>As more states, countries and corporations adopt more flexible and inclusive leave policies, researchers will continue to learn how parental leave benefits both parents and children. What they’ve found so far leads me to believe that, just like we’ve seen with <a href="https://heartlandforward.org/research/the-economic-case-for-investing-in-maternal-health/#the-economic-impacts">prenatal care</a> and <a href="https://nhsa.org/about-nhsa/our-impact/">early education programs</a>, parental leave will prove to be an early investment in healthy children and families that pays dividends in the long term.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/290773/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

<title>Menopause is a major health milestone, yet health records barely track it - new research</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/762207/original/file-20260925-58-33x2rw.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=0%2C1%2C7874%2C5249&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">There is enormous variation in how menopause unfolds across different people.</span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/photo/happy-woman-spending-leisure-time-with-friends-at-royalty-free-image/2247267966">Morsa Images/DigitalVision via Getty Images</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>Anyone with ovaries who lives long enough will <a href="https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/menopause/what-menopause">experience menopause</a>. While menopause is a natural transition in midlife, it can strongly <a href="https://doi.org/10.1089/jwh.2012.3719">affect a person’s quality of life</a> and their current and future <a href="https://orwh.od.nih.gov/menopause-midlife-health">risk of heart disease, osteoporosis and other issues</a>. So you might think that whether someone is experiencing or has gone through menopause would be noted in their medical records.</p>

<p>But when we and our colleagues examined the electronic medical records of almost 240,000 women, only <a href="https://doi.org/10.1097/GME.0000000000002884">12% included mention of menopause</a>, even though more than half the women reported separately that they were experiencing this transition. Our findings, published in the journal Menopause, reveal a major gap in how clinicians capture basic information about women’s health. </p>

<p>The menopausal women we examined are from a broader group of 400,000 who  participated in the <a href="https://www.nih.gov/allofus">All of Us Research Program</a>, a nationwide study run by the National Institutes of Health to compile a <a href="https://www.researchallofus.org/data-tools/data-snapshots/?_gl=1*1rsb3hx*_ga*MTYxMjU1NzkxOS4xNzg3NTk2ODI4*_ga_MQVR5DG2C4*czE3OTAyODE4MjgkbzMkZzEkdDE3OTAyODE4NDgkajQwJGwwJGgxMzM0MDcyNDg4">wide range of health data</a> from at least 1 million Americans. We looked at how information about menopause was included in electronic health records and how this information differed by demographics, such as age, education, race and income. </p>

<p>Because study participants filled out health surveys upon enrolling, we could track discrepancies between their own reports of menopause and what was in their medical records. Age at menopause and symptoms, such as hot flashes or sleep disturbances, were also largely missing from the medical records and survey. </p>



<h2>Missing links</h2>

<p><a href="https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2014.8063">Many aspects of menopause</a>, and the <a href="https://doi.org/10.1001/jamacardio.2016.2415">diversity in women’s experiences</a> with it, remain poorly understood.</p>

<p>For example, when menopause begins, as well as how disruptive its symptoms are, <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ogc.2011.05.001">can vary greatly</a>. Some women experience extreme hot flashes, sleep disruptions and brain fog, while others do not. One woman may go through natural menopause at age 45, and another at 54. Both ages would be considered normal, but that timing can affect current and future health in distinct ways. </p>

<figure>
            <iframe width="440" height="260" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/cheqkrcHkrI?wmode=transparent&amp;start=0" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>
            <figcaption><span class="caption">Menopause is a natural transition in midlife, but it can strongly affect current and future health risks.</span></figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Electronic medical records <a href="https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-publhealth-032315-021353">offer an unmatched opportunity</a> to investigate these knowledge gaps, enabling researchers to study the experience of hundreds of thousands or even millions of people using routinely collected data. </p>

<p>Such large-scale studies may shed light on how menopause symptoms change over time and who is more likely to experience them; how markers of heart disease, bone health or mental health track with menopause; how social determinants of health, such as ethnicity and access to healthcare, affect someone’s lived experience of menopause; and countless other unanswered questions.</p>

<h2>Closing the data gap</h2>

<p>Our study is not the first to point out how inconsistently menopause status and symptoms are recorded in <a href="https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.23217">healthcare settings</a> and <a href="https://doi.org/10.1097/GME.0000000000002868">electronic health records</a>. But it systematically highlights the enormity of the gap, showing that menopause is often not even recorded at all.</p>

<p>It’s not clear why menopause is so rarely documented in electronic health records. It may be because menopause is not a disease, so it does not generally occur to clinicians to note it as a diagnostic code. It may feel obvious or irrelevant to diagnose or measure. It’s possible that patients themselves often don’t bring it up unless their symptoms are severe. Healthcare providers routinely ask middle-aged patients about their reproductive health – for example, when they had their last menstrual period – but this information rarely ends up getting documented in the electronic health record. </p>

<p>As we see it, not capturing this information is a colossal missed opportunity to drive vital research and improve personalized healthcare. Our team is developing a short, simple questionnaire about menopause status and symptoms for patients to fill out as they check in for medical appointments. These responses could then be added to their medical records for use by both their healthcare team and researchers. We are also developing a computer-based approach to infer menopause-related information from other data in a woman’s health record or genetics. </p>

<p>Finally, we are exploring the All of Us dataset to identify systematic differences – for example, in patients’ cultural background or income level, specific health system practices, urban versus rural settings – that might be linked with whether menopause data gets recorded in medical records. These associations can point to targeted ways to encourage its collection. </p>

<p>It’s impossible to research, and treat, what’s not measured. Capturing the menopause transition is an essential step to improving healthcare for women in midlife.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/292227/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

<p><em><a href="https://theconversation.com/topics/curious-kids-us-74795">Curious Kids</a> is a series for children of all ages. If you have a question you’d like an expert to answer, send it to <a href="mailto:curiouskidsus@theconversation.com">CuriousKidsUS@theconversation.com</a>.</em></p>

<hr>

<blockquote>
<p><strong>What was the first “first-person shooter” video game? 
– James, age 12, Batesville, Arkansas</strong></p>
</blockquote>

<hr>

<p>Before “<a href="https://callofduty.fandom.com/wiki/Call_of_Duty_(series)">Call of Duty</a>,” before “<a href="https://skinrave.gg/en/blog/the-complete-history-of-counter-strike-full-timeline">Counter-Strike</a>” and before “<a href="https://www.britannica.com/topic/Doom">Doom</a>,” there was “<a href="https://www.acmi.net.au/works/60826--maze-war/">Maze War</a>.” </p>

<p>Generally considered the earliest first-person shooter game, or FPS, “Maze War” was developed at a NASA research center beginning in 1973. A year later, another FPS, “<a href="https://www.tycoonstory.com/what-was-the-first-fps-game/">Spasim</a>,” debuted. It was developed at the University of Illinois.</p>

<p>In first-person shooters, players experience the game through the eyes of a character, using a gun or other weapon to attack enemies. To pull off this first-person perspective, developers needed to create a 3D world for the players to move through – no easy feat in the early 1970s.</p>

<p>At the time, the computer hardware behind the most popular arcade game, “<a href="https://computerhistory.org/blog/50-years-of-fun-with-pong/">PONG</a>,” and the first home video game system, the <a href="https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20231213-in-history-the-first-ever-video-game-console-50-years-on">Magnavox Odyssey</a>, wasn’t powerful enough to render the kind of 3D depth that allowed players to move forward into a virtual space, with objects appearing in the distance.</p>

<figure class="align-right zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A vintage desktop computer from the 1970s with a small, narrow screen and a keyboard attached to it." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=237&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=417&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=417&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=417&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=524&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=524&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760863/original/file-20260918-50-cg7oj8.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=524&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">‘Maze War’ was developed on the Imlac PDS-1.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/57/Imlac_PDS-1_1969.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=index&amp;utm_content=original">Electronics/Wikimedia Commons</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>That’s why both games were developed on systems that had more processing power and speed. “Maze War” first appeared on an <a href="https://gunkies.org/wiki/IMLAC_PDS-1">Imlac PDS-1 minicomputer</a>, while “Spasim” – short for “space simulator” – launched on <a href="https://gunkies.org/wiki/PLATO">PLATO</a>, an early networked computer system. </p>

<p>Since everyday people couldn’t easily access the Imlac PDS-1 minicomputer or PLATO, these two games have been largely forgotten. But they paved the way for <a href="https://rocketbrush.com/blog/most-popular-video-game-genres-revenue-statistics-genres-overview">one of today’s most popular video game genres</a>.</p>

<h2>Out of sight, but not out of mind</h2>

<p>Both games allowed players to move through a 3D space and shoot enemy figures that appeared onscreen in the player’s view.  </p>

<p>In “Spasim,” movement and shooting didn’t occur in real time. You moved by jumping from one position to another, with a short lag time needed to render the next view.</p>

<p>In “Maze War,” players could move relatively smoothly in a straight line down hallways. Turning, however, needed to be done in 90-degree increments, which created some potentially confusing graphics as entire scenes abruptly appeared. In the single-player mode, danger could lurk just around the corner: Robots would automatically shoot you if they were in line with you down a hallway.</p>

<p>“Maze War” and “Spasim” also had multiplayer modes that allowed networked players to shoot at each other. Before video games, <a href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/shot-in-the-rifle-in-the-carnival-france-on-1950s-rv-234900-news-photo/55753064?adppopup=true">popular shooting games</a> – the kind found at fairs and carnivals – generally involved friendly competition, with players competing to see who could hit targets most accurately. The kill-or-be-killed death matches of “Maze War” and “Spasim” completely upended the way guns were used in play and competition.</p>

<figure>
            <iframe width="440" height="260" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/9wX5L03r-qA?wmode=transparent&amp;start=0" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>
            <figcaption><span class="caption">In ‘Maze War,’ players are required to turn in 90-degree increments.</span></figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>‘Maze War’ introduced another new twist: the possibility of getting shot at and killed from behind, without ever seeing your attacker. Instead of the fixed and unchanging point of view found in a shooting gallery, ‘Maze War’ required you to constantly look around to try to keep track of everything in your immediate area. </p>

<p>And unlike most video games up to this point, players didn’t see the entirety of a game’s world from a godlike perspective. Instead, there was a sense of offscreen space surrounding the player, with events occurring out of the player’s sight.</p>

<h2>Building a 3D world with lines</h2>

<p>Both ‘Maze War’ and ‘Spasim’ used what are called <a href="https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VectorGame">vector graphics</a>, which are images made by drawing lines directly between points on the screen. </p>

<p>Compared with the other popular form of computer graphics, known as <a href="https://www.britannica.com/technology/raster-graphics">raster graphics</a>, <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swryO4xWOTk">vector graphics were particularly well suited</a> for creating a first-person perspective. They contain clean lines that converge at a vanishing point, making a flat screen appear to stretch into the distance. Raster graphics, on the other hand, create pictures by filling in a grid of tiny pixels, an approach that was less suited to drawing the crisp lines needed to create this kind of perspective.</p>

<figure class="align-center ">
            <img alt="A demonstration of how lines can create vanishing points." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=378&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=378&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=378&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=474&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=474&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/760876/original/file-20260918-50-7da4yh.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=474&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px">
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Diagonal lines create vanishing points that make a flat surface appear to stretch into the distance.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/44/1ptPerspective.svg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=index&amp;utm_content=original">InkScape/Wikimedia Commons</a>, <a class="license" href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>By 1977, video game fans could play Cinematronic’s “<a href="https://thedoteaters.com/?bitstory=bitstory-article-2/space-wars-and-cinematronics">Space Wars</a>,” which used vector graphics, at arcades. In 1978, Vectorbeam’s “<a href="https://www.arcade-museum.com/Videogame/speed-freak">Speed Freak</a>” deployed vector graphics to render the first real-time, 3D computer animation in an arcade video game – <a href="https://kotaku.com/games/speed-freak">an explosion of car parts when the player crashed</a>. Atari’s 1980 arcade game “<a href="https://www.arcade-museum.com/Videogame/battlezone">Battlezone</a>” was a huge hit that gave many players their first chance to try a first-person shooting game.</p>

<p>“Maze War” and “Spasim” didn’t have the aiming capabilities that players are used to today. Shooting was done with a keystroke, with aiming limited to facing in the right direction. Nor did they have the speed, spectacle and realism of their modern descendants. But they introduced something more fundamental: a new way of seeing and experiencing a video game.</p>

In 1978, Vectorbeam’s “ Speed Freak ” deployed vector graphics to render the first real-time, 3D computer animation in an arcade video game – an explosion of car parts when the player crashed

Atari’s 1980 arcade game “ Battlezone ” was a huge hit that gave many players their first chance to try a first-person shooting game. “Maze War” and “Spasim” didn’t have the aiming capabilities that players are used to today
Shooting was done with a keystroke, with aiming limited to facing in the right direction
Nor did they have the speed, spectacle and realism of their modern descendants
But they introduced something more fundamental: a new way of seeing and experiencing a video game

title: Trump’s taxpayer-funded propaganda blitz
